Requires `recipient_lookup`. Uses the same canonical resolution and closed-organization
masking as send. This does not send a message or change contacts, threads or admission.

before the first send; a retry must use the saved request rather than resolving a handle again.

item.name: events
item.description: Server-Sent Events stream.

item.name: Server-Sent Events stream for an account

query.description: `1` opts this client into typed events (ids like `"<mail>.<n>"`). Group events are re-authorized against current membership at delivery.
Resume cursor, for clients that cannot set headers. Either a mail cursor (`"123"`) or a typed cursor (`"123.4"`).

request.description:
One stream per account covering all of its mailboxes. Only metadata crosses the stream,
never message bodies. Keep-alive comments are sent every 15 seconds. Without a resume
cursor the stream starts at "now".

**Event types**

* `mail` — legacy format, unchanged. The `id:` line is the message cursor (a decimal
  integer). Data: `{event_id: integer, mailbox, message_id, sender, created_at}`.
* Typed events — sent when the `account_events` feature flag is enabled for the
  account, or when the client asks with `typed=1` (Phase 3a: `group.*`, `mls.*`,
  `message.expired`, `thread.settings`; see docs/groups.md §4). The `id:` line is `"<mail_cursor>.<event_seq>"`. Data:
  `{event_id: string, type: string, mailbox: string|null, data: object}`. Initial type:
  `features.changed` with data `{feature, enabled}`.
* `resync_required` — no `id:` line. Data
  `{type: "resync_required", reason: "cursor_expired"}`. Sent when the resume cursor is older
  than the retained window (7 days / 10,000 events per account). The client must reload
  authoritative state (inbox, threads, capabilities) and then continue from the new ids.

Clients must ignore event types they do not recognise.

item.name: mcp
item.description: Model Context Protocol endpoints (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP).

request.description:
Methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `ping`, `tools/call`. The bearer token is optional for
`initialize`/`tools/list`; tool calls authenticate with a capability token, an account API
key or a member token. Tool failures (including authentication failures) are reported as
error tool-results inside a 200 JSON-RPC response, not as HTTP errors. A notification
(no `id`) gets an empty 202.

JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP endpoint exposing a restricted tool set. Tool calls require an OAuth access
token whose audience is this resource and that carries the `pigeonpost:read` or
`pigeonpost:write` scope. Requests from browser origins other than ChatGPT/OpenAI are refused
with 403. Unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` header values get 400. Missing or invalid
tokens get 401 (insufficient scope 403) with a JSON-RPC body carrying an
`mcp/www_authenticate` challenge. Body limit 128 KiB.
